title: Adaptive Apply Safeguard for Optimize Recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an adaptive, operator-visible safeguard layer for automatically applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + caching configuration changes). The safeguard must: 1) run a deterministic simulation of candidate configs against a recent production trace; 2) perform a staged canary rollout policy (simulation -> dry-run traffic -> small real traffic -> scale up) with explicit metric gates; 3) expose approval hooks in Console for operator override and forced rollbacks; 4) record audit events and create reversible diffs so changes can be rolled back atomically. Goal is to allow low-risk auto-adoption of high-confidence cost-saving configs while keeping safety and on-call controls intact.
acceptance_criteria: A simulation harness that replays at least 1 hour of production traffic and reports token-cost delta, p50/p95/p99 latency delta, and quality regression estimate per config
A canary controller that will apply a config to N% of traffic with automatic progression only if all metric gates pass
Console shows a proposal card with simulation results, estimated monthly savings, suggested rollout plan, and an approval button
All applied changes are recorded as a reversible config diff with a single-click rollback in Console and via API
Operational playbook created and exercised in staging; runbook validated with a simulated failure causing an automatic rollback
implementation_notes: Build simulation harness as an isolated job that consumes anonymized request traces from recent telemetry (prefix+length histograms and representative payload samples)
Use existing batching runtime hooks to instrument expected per-request cost under candidate batch sizes and cache hit rates
Canary controller integrates with smart-routing: initial dry-run mode (no effect on real tokens) -> shadowed small-percentage traffic -> gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%)
Gates are evaluated every 10 minutes; failures trigger immediate halt and rollback with telemetry snapshot attached
Config diffs stored in git-like immutable store with hashes so we can validate no drift during apply/rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulation (automated) — generate simulation report and confidence score
Phase 1: Operator review (optional) — Console shows results and suggests approval; can be set to auto-approve for high-confidence scores
Phase 2: Dry-run (shadow) for 30 minutes against 1% of traffic, collect signals
Phase 3: Canary real traffic 5% for 1 hour, evaluate gates
Phase 4: Incremental expansion 25% for 2 hours, then 100% if stable
Phase 5: Post-apply monitoring window of 48 hours with elevated alerting and rollback window
gating_thresholds: Token cost reduction must be >= 3% in simulation to be considered for auto-apply
p99 latency regression must be < 5% relative and absolute increase < 50ms
Error rate (model errors / serving errors) must not increase by more than 0.05 percentage points
Quality regression estimated by eval harness must be below thresholds: BLEU-like/semantic-similarity drop < 0.5% (configurable by model category)
Any single critical SLO breach during a gate window fails the gate
monitoring_signals: KV cache hit rate and prefix hit distribution
end-to-end quality metric from eval-set scoring and sampled human review
rollback_playbook: Automatic rollback: if any gate fails, canary controller immediately reverts the changed config for affected shards and escalates to on-call
Manual rollback: Console exposes single-click revert with rationale field and optional postmortem template
Rollback telemetry snapshot is stored for postmortem analysis (pre-apply and post-apply state)
If rollback fails due to drift/lock, open a high-priority incident and surface a read-only fallback variant
Post-rollback: run targeted simulation to validate that rollback restored baseline metrics

2026-03-10: Integration test failed on shadow mode due to rate-limiter interaction; added backpressure handling and retry windows (Miguel)
2026-03-12: Canary controller MVP can progress 0%->5%->25% and aborts when p99 exceeds set threshold (testing in staging passed)
decisions: Use simulation-first flow rather than relying solely on live shadow traffic to reduce risk and operator load
Tie auto-approval to a confidence score computed from ensemble of simulation metrics + historical outcome models
Store all applied configs as immutable diffs in the existing config-store; do not mutate in place
Make the default for high-risk routes 'operator approval required' and allow customers to opt-in to auto-apply for low-risk routes
risks: Simulation mismatch risk: production patterns may diverge causing unexpected regressions
Quality regressions not visible in automated evals may still impact user experience
Race conditions between autoscaler changes and canary controller could amplify transient latency spikes
Operator alert fatigue if thresholds are too sensitive leading to frequent manual interventions
qa_plan: Unit tests for diff store and atomic apply/rollback
Integration tests in staging with synthetic traffic trace and fault injection
Chaos test: simulate a sudden spike in latency during canary to verify automatic rollback
User acceptance test with two pilot customers in Dedicated mode (consent required)
notes_for_oncall: Alert: AdaptiveApply.CanaryAbort — triggered when any gate fails during canary
Runbook step: verify config diff hash, examine pre/post telemetry snapshot, perform revert if auto-rollback did not succeed
If drift detected, pin traffic to baseline and open incident with 'canary-drift' tag
